lines.style: Speak fluent, casual General American English to a friend who is staring at a phone with no reply: gently teasing, a knowing little smile in the voice, stress on "ghosted", falling intonation. Quick, about one and a half seconds.
Speak English as a confused friend who just heard the word and wonders if it means a real ghost: one word, puzzled, rising question intonation, a little slow. About one second.
Speak fluent, natural General American English, clear and friendly, like saying a new slang word for a learner: one word, falling intonation. About one second.

lines.text: I didn't mean to ghost you; my phone broke.
lines.style: Speak fluent, casual General American English to a friend, apologetic and a little sheepish: a short beat after "ghost you", stress on "ghost" and "broke". Natural pace, about two and a half seconds.
